summary: The purpose of our project is to help children from 7 to 12 years of age to gain knowledge and develop valuable skills about basic functions performed by astronauts on missions, by developing the game based on real missions performed by NASA on the Planet Mars. Consisting of several chapters the objective is to do extensive research about the rocks and resources found on the Planet to deepen their understanding while taking care of vital needs like water and oxygen supplies. It is essential to show people how exciting this field can be.
details:
What does it do?
Mission Trainer is a browser game where you’re a young astronaut keeping a Mars outpost alive. You land the rocket, set up the base, and fix problems in hands-on tasks: patch an air leak, repair the water filter, clean dust off the solar panels, identify rocks, and choose a route for the rover. The route choice uses real NASA Mars Trek data from Jezero Crater: a short, steep road over a hill, or a longer, safer road around it. The game shows what your choice costs.

Benefits
Kids learn real mission trade-offs by doing, not by reading. It runs in any web browser with nothing to install, so it works in classrooms and at home.

Intended impact
We want kids to see that space missions are about smart trade-offs, and to get curious about real missions like Perseverance.

Tools
HTML, CSS and JavaScript (Canvas for graphics; every sound made in code with the Web Audio API), Python, NASA Mars Trek data, NASA JPL’s rover route guide, WebStorm, Git and GitHub.

Creativity
Every science idea is something you do, like following a scanner signal to find a leak or watching the rover struggle up the hill you picked. Real orbital data becomes a choice a 10-year-old can make.

Factors considered
Kids’ attention spans, scientific accuracy (real NASA numbers only), simple language, keyboard and touch controls, and making both route choices fair trade-offs instead of a trick question.
